build.snapshot: a full key generation by compactc 0.35.0 of a contract tree whose ZKIR is byte-identical to 19e0762's, circuit by circuit
build.note: The sections grants, grantee-scope-U, grantee-scope-S, grantee-scope-C, frame-lifecycle, readability, rules, module, hints, arm-asserts, display-module ran at 19e0762 on these keys. devices ran at f143be8 and activation, seam, replay, frame, custody, witness, recovery, field-rendering at 5efb61f, earlier revisions of this arm before the commits of this history were cut: each of their cases equals the case of the same name in the DRY at 19e0762 (circuit, kind, expected refusal, bypassed asserts, enforcement), and every proof-server request they made named the verifier key that these keys hold for its circuit, so no key they used has changed; none of them proves issue_grant_with_sol_ed25519, the one circuit whose key changed since. Every negative names its positive control (results[].control): its own, in the run's record, or one proved earlier in the same run through the same patched module file for the same circuit, named by the runs that record it and, for the earlier runs, derived from the run's own data by that rule. A negative of a check of the verification inputs or of a readable format, and every negative of hints, arm-asserts and display-module, has its own. One run per section (grantee-scope once per grantee twin), each on a freshly restarted proof server.

method: Each negative runs twice: in the simulator (the generated JavaScript, honest checks) and at the proof server with the JavaScript checks that would refuse it bypassed in a patched copy of the generated contract (and, where a value the runtime refuses must reach the transcript, named runtime functions overridden); each copy first proves the admissible call of the same circuit through itself, and each negative names the control its refusal is attributed to. A case passes only when it is refused at the expected layer and the refusal is attributed to the circuit under test.
